concept.name: Feature
concept.definition: An input variable supplied to a statistical or machine-learning model, derived from raw observations without using future information.
concept.intuition: It controls what information the model receives and in what numerical representation.
concept.mechanics: Define its timestamp and lookback, fit any transformation on training data, and construct the same value identically in validation and live use.
concept.failure_modes: Fitting the operation on the full dataset leaks future information; revisions, outliers, and missing values can also distort results.
concept.misconceptions: A cleaner or rescaled dataset is not automatically more truthful; transformations must preserve timing and economic meaning.
concept.example: At each close, 20-day realized volatility computed through that close is a feature for predicting next-day range.
